thread:
erin: Quick heads-up — I updated the capacity runway model with Q3->Q4 seasonal surge scenarios. Putting the PDF in the S3 link but wanted quick sync here. main ask: can we confirm H200 availability assumptions for APAC?
ryan: saw the doc, nice. what's the delta vs our prior lead-time assumptions?
sam: short answer: H200 lead times slipped ~6–9 weeks from the vendor's latest note. that impacts our reservation window for Nov traffic. :grimacing:
erin: ouch. can you paste the vendor note or key lines?
sam: pasted snippet from procurement thread: 
```
Vendor update (3/2): Allocations for H200 series are constrained; estimated shipment lead-time 10-14 weeks for new orders. L40S still available with 6-9 week lead. H100 limited to refurb/resale channels only.
```
chen: given that, we should run 3 scenarios in the model: conservative (no new H200), balanced (partial H200 reserve + L40S fallback), aggressive (reserve H200 + on-demand bursts). I pushed a branch with scenario toggles.
julia: @chen where's the branch? I want to run cost delta reports for the balanced scenario.
chen: https://git.internal/repo/capacity-runway branch `scenario/balanced-mix` — includes regional splits.
erin: high-level numbers from my run: 
```
Baseline  (current fleet):  120k GPU-hours/month
Scenario A (Q4 +30%):     156k GPU-hours/month
Equivalent nodes needed (H200): ~130 units
Equivalent nodes needed (L40S): ~210 units
Cost delta (balanced): +18% monthly infra spend
```
ryan: important to note H200 throughput per dollar is better for latency-critical workloads. swapping to L40S increases cost for the same p50 latency targets.
sam: agree — but if lead times block H200, we can use L40S with more aggressive caching and batching to preserve p50 within SLOs. need ops playbook changes.
erin: ops checklist idea:
- Canary pool: reserve 10% capacity as dedicated H100/H200 mix for canaries
- Fallback policy: route non-critical bursts to L40S or regional low-cost pool
- Autoscale caps: hard cap to prevent runaway spend during experiments
ryan: also consider contract options: 6 month reservation vs spot + burst. procurement says reserves buy priority but tie up cash.
chen: I'll add a tradeoff table in the branch. need input on region constraints: APAC has limited H200 allocation — we should bias reservations to US-EAST and EU-WEST and plan cross-region routing.
julia: for customer-facing SLAs, do we plan to advertise region-specific performance if we shift capacity? customers may expect uniform latency.
erin: we'll default to regional SLOs and add a config flag to pin to region. docs/console will show availability by region.
sam: one more quick calc I ran for throughput projection: 
```
Assume: 120k baseline, 30% seasonal demand spike, 20% reduction via caching/better batching
Net demand = 120k * 1.3 * 0.8 = 124.8k GPU-hours -> about +4% vs baseline
```
That shows optimizations buy a lot.
ryan: nice. can infra team run a short health check script across clusters to estimate reclaimable capacity before committing purchases? simple `kubectl` shard-level checks + eviction-safe pods list.
erin: @infra-bot can you kick off the reclaimability scan and post a short report in this thread when done?
infra-bot: Scheduled reclaim scan started. Will post results in ~30m.
erin: thanks. action items: 
- chen: add region bias and tradeoff table to branch (due EOD)
- sam: share full vendor note + suggestions for ops playbook (due tomorrow)
- ryan: work with procurement on reservation vs burst modeling (due 3/10)
- infra-bot: post reclaim scan results here
julia: +1. I'll prepare customer messaging drafts once we lock the region/availability plan.
erin: cool — keeping this thread as the single source for decisions. will update the model after reclaim scan. :thumbsup:
